children: Intuitive Surgical
shares fell sharply after hours despite beating Wall Street expectations for the third quarter, as investors focused on a
$450 million antitrust settlement
and a more measured growth outlook.
The robotic-surgery leader reported
$3.05 billion in Q3 revenue
, up 22% from $2.51 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings reached
$3.00 per share
, compared with $2.40 in the prior-year quarter.
Operationally, the quarter was strong.
Worldwide procedures across da Vinci and Ion platforms increased about
, with da Vinci procedures up roughly 14% and Ion procedures rising 31%.
Intuitive also placed
546 da Vinci systems
, up from 427 a year earlier. Of those, 315 were the newer da Vinci 5 platform.
But the headline beat was overshadowed by litigation.
Intuitive agreed to pay
$450 million
to settle previously disclosed antitrust class-action litigation tied to its da Vinci business. The company did not admit liability or wrongdoing, and the agreement still requires court approval.
The charge reduced GAAP earnings materially.
Intuitive reported GAAP net income of
$523 million, or $1.49 per diluted share
, down from $704 million, or $1.95 per share, a year ago. The settlement reduced after-tax income by $347 million, or
$0.99 per share
Investor Takeaway
I think the market reaction says investors were looking for more than a clean earnings beat.
The core business continues to perform well, with strong procedure growth, rising da Vinci 5 placements and expanding recurring instrument revenue.
But the $450 million settlement introduces a large one-time cost, while investors are also watching whether procedure growth can maintain its current pace as competition in robotic surgery increases.
For investors, the key things to watch are
da Vinci procedure growth, da Vinci 5 adoption, Ion growth, system placements and whether legal or competitive pressures begin affecting margins or utilization
The underlying quarter was strong.
The issue is that expectations for Intuitive Surgical remain high enough that even a solid beat may not be enough when a major legal charge and softer forward signals arrive at the same time.

title: Intuitive Surgical Drops as $450 Million Charge Overshadows Beat
